title: Claude Certified Architect - Question Bank Schema

tier_1.label: Conceptual Knowledge (Recall)
tier_1.description: Tests whether the candidate knows a fact, definition, or rule from the exam content
indicators: Which of the following describes X?
Which flag / setting / configuration achieves X?

tier_2.label: Applied Judgment (Application)
tier_2.description: Tests whether the candidate can apply knowledge to a realistic production scenario and choose the correct action
indicators: Given this production context, what should you do?
Which approach best addresses this problem?
What is the most effective first step?

tier_3.label: Anti-Pattern Recognition (Analysis)
tier_3.description: Tests whether the candidate can identify incorrect, risky, or suboptimal approaches — including options that sound plausible but violate best practices
indicators: Which option introduces a reliability risk?
A colleague proposes X — what is the flaw?
What is the most likely root cause of this failure?

scenarios.title: Customer Support Resolution Agent
scenarios.context: Building a customer support resolution agent using the Claude Agent SDK. The agent handles high-ambiguity requests like returns, billing disputes, and account issues. MCP tools: get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human. Target: 80%+ first-contact resolution.

scenarios.title: Code Generation with Claude Code
scenarios.context: Using Claude Code to accelerate software development: code generation, refactoring, debugging, documentation. Integrating custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md configurations, plan mode vs direct execution.

scenarios.title: Multi-Agent Research System
scenarios.context: Building a multi-agent research system using Claude Agent SDK. Coordinator delegates to: web search agent, document analysis agent, synthesis agent, report generation agent. Produces comprehensive cited reports.

scenarios.title: Developer Productivity with Claude
scenarios.context: Building developer productivity tools with Claude Agent SDK. Agent explores unfamiliar codebases, understands legacy systems, generates boilerplate, automates repetitive tasks. Uses built-in tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob + MCP servers.

scenarios.title: Claude Code for Continuous Integration
scenarios.context: Integrating Claude Code into CI/CD pipeline. System runs automated code reviews, generates test cases, provides PR feedback. Requires prompts for actionable feedback and minimal false positives.

scenarios.title: Structured Data Extraction
scenarios.context: Building a structured data extraction system using Claude. Extracts information from unstructured documents, validates via JSON schemas, maintains high accuracy, handles edge cases gracefully, integrates with downstream systems.

scenario_ids: array — primary and any recombined scenario IDs e.g. S1, S3
question_template.key_concept_tested: string — specific concept from task statement key_concepts list
question_template.stem: string — the question text, framed within the scenario context
question_template.explanation: string — explains why correct is right AND why each distractor is wrong

distractor_strategy.plausible_but_prompt_only: option that sounds correct but relies on probabilistic LLM compliance
distractor_strategy.over_engineered: option that would work but adds unnecessary infrastructure
distractor_strategy.wrong_layer: option that addresses a real problem but the wrong one
distractor_strategy.valid_but_not_first_step: option correct in principle but premature given the scenario

tags: array of searchable tags e.g. stop_reason, tool_choice, hooks, CLAUDE.md

scenario_recombination_rules: Each question must reference at least one scenario from the scenarios list
Cross-scenario questions (combinable_with) should make up ~20% of each batch
Do not reuse the same scenario+task_statement+difficulty combination within a batch
Rotate correct answer position (A/B/C/D) to avoid pattern bias — no label should appear >40% in a batch
distractor_rules: Every distractor must represent a genuine misconception or incomplete knowledge — not obviously wrong
At least one distractor per question should be a prompt-only / probabilistic compliance anti-pattern
At least one distractor should be over-engineered (adds infrastructure when a simpler fix exists)
Distractors must be plausible to a candidate with 3-5 months experience but insufficient for production
stem_variation_rules: Vary question framing: 'What should you do?', 'What is the root cause?', 'Why is this insufficient?', 'Which option introduces risk?'
Mix positive framing ('best approach') with negative framing ('most likely to fail')
Include production metrics in stems where relevant (e.g. '12% failure rate', '40% latency increase')
Reference specific API constructs (stop_reason, tool_choice, isError) in stems for applied/anti-pattern tiers

generation_prompt_template: Generate a batch of {batch_size} exam questions for the Claude Certified Architect – Foundations exam. Focus on domain {domain_id} ({domain_name}), task statements {task_statement_ids}. Use scenarios {scenario_ids} as context, recombining where marked combinable_with. Apply difficulty distribution: {pct_conceptual}% conceptual_knowledge, {pct_applied}% applied_judgment, {pct_antipattern}% anti_pattern_recognition. Output each question as a JSON object matching the question_template schema. Vary correct answer position across the batch. Each distractor must reflect a genuine production misconception. Include explanation that addresses all four options.
